candidates.statement: For all ordinary rooted binary trees T,U on the same X, and all cherries {a,b} in T that are not cherries in U, there exists a minimum agreement forest for T,U containing singleton {a} or singleton {b}.
candidates.motivation: If true this would permit discarding the branch that cuts every off-path subtree in the standard rooted cherry rule.
candidates.failure_criterion: A pair and cherry such that every minimum agreement forest contains neither {a} nor {b} as a singleton.
candidates.search: All ordered pairs of canonical labelled trees for n=3,4; only extend after measured pilot.

candidates.statement: For all ordinary rooted binary trees T,U on X and every S subset X with |S|>=2 and equal rooted restrictions T|S=U|S, retaining any one s in S and deleting S minus {s} from both trees preserves the optimum number of agreement-forest components.
candidates.motivation: This tempting over-extension of common-pendant-subtree reduction would allow much more aggressive kernelization.
candidates.failure_criterion: Optimum(T,U) != Optimum(T|(X minus (S minus {s})), U|(X minus (S minus {s}))).
candidates.search: Conflicting-triple hand control, then all small pairs as needed.

status_semantics: Passing finite tests never proves the universal statement. A complete exact counterexample refutes it; certificate remains computational until independent replay and Lean formalization.
